title: The disc becomes a pear

objective.text: Describe how the embryonic disc changes shape during week 3.

body.general: Why does the round disc turn into a pear? It grows from about 0.2 mm to over 1 mm in a few days [f4]. Most of the growth is at the head end, fed by cells streaming forward from the streak [f2]. So the disc becomes broad at the head end and narrow at the tail end [f1]. The head end starts forming its parts in mid-week 3, while the tail end is still gastrulating until the end of week 4 [f3].
body.mbbs: During week 3 the flat, almost round disc elongates into a pear shape: broad cranially, narrow caudally [f1]. Growth is mainly cranial, supplied by cells migrating forward from the streak; the streak region stays about the same size [f2]. The disc grows from about 0.2 mm at days 14–15 to about 1.25 mm by day 18 [f4]. Cranial structures begin to differentiate by mid-week 3, while gastrulation continues caudally until the end of week 4 [f3]. Development therefore runs in a cranial-to-caudal direction [f5].

facts.text: The flat, nearly round disc grows into a pear shape: broad at the head end, narrow at the tail end.
Most growth is at the head end, fed by cells streaming forward from the streak; the streak region stays about the same size.
Head structures start to form in mid-week 3, while the tail end is still gastrulating until the end of week 4.
So the embryo develops head end first.
The disc grows from about 0.2 mm on days 14–15 to about 1.25 mm by day 18.

misconceptions.wrong: Gastrulation is over by the end of week 3.
misconceptions.right: It goes on at the tail end until the end of week 4.

misconceptions.wrong: The disc grows evenly all over.
misconceptions.right: Most growth is at the head end; the streak region stays about the same size.

checks.why: Growth is mostly cranial, so the head end broadens into a pear shape.

checks.prompt: Until when does gastrulation go on at the tail end?
checks.why: The caudal end is still gastrulating until the end of week 4, after the head end has started to differentiate.

adult: This head-first lead is why the head end of the embryo takes shape before the tail end [f3,f5].
